project.name: example-ea-sbm
project.description: Sanitized example of a paper-experiment recovery profile.

method_exploration.purpose: Explore candidate method ideas before committing them to row-level recovery.
entry_conditions: a row family lacks a mature candidate route
baseline evidence suggests a method gap but target thresholds are not yet actionable
a small prototype or ablation can test a new research hypothesis cheaply
allowed_actions: identify one method gap or hypothesis
design a bounded prototype, ablation, or smoke-scale evaluation
implement minimal code/config changes inside writable workspaces
promote, revise, or reject candidate method routes
required_artifacts: promote, revise, reject, or continue decision
updated status, journal, and lane ledger
success_criteria: one candidate method becomes more or less credible using evidence
the next row-recovery or validation step is more specific than before
the agent avoids broad undirected metric search
escalation_criteria: the method idea requires data or domain context outside configured workspaces
no bounded prototype can test the hypothesis
the proposed direction would require broad model redesign beyond one cycle

audit_validation.purpose: Audit uncertain experiment chains before treating them as recovery evidence.
entry_conditions: row provenance, metric mapping, leakage risk, or runner behavior is unclear
a candidate needs a narrow validation before full-row execution
completed evidence may not be comparable to target rows
allowed_actions: candidate package design without launching if evidence is insufficient
success_criteria: the uncertainty blocking a target row is reduced
the next action is a specific candidate, blocker, or follow-up audit
unsafe or incomparable evidence is not promoted
escalation_criteria: evidence needed for the audit is outside available workspaces
the next validation would risk leakage or overwrite evidence

target_recovery.purpose: Recover predefined paper/table rows with reproducible evidence.
entry_conditions: target rows and primary metrics are defined
the next useful action can be tied to a specific row or row family
allowed_actions: rank open rows by target gap and urgency
launch full or remaining-fold row packages
launch upstream/unblocking tasks when a row is not ready
update row state from aggregate evidence
required_artifacts: selected target row or row family
hypothesis, command, output root, and log path
updated status, journal, and row/lane ledger
success_criteria: an open row receives a concrete push or a documented true blocker
a failed candidate does not close the row
evidence is recorded with metric/provenance caveats
escalation_criteria: all open rows require external information
primary metrics or target thresholds are ambiguous
the next recovery step would risk leakage or overwrite evidence
